text.p: --BIRTHDAYS--
Founder of the "Sydney Morning Herald" JOHN FAIRFAX was born in 1804. He migrated to Australia after a libel suit sent him broke in England.
Austrian composer JOHANN STRAUSS THE YOUNGER, who wrote the popular waltz "The Blue Danube", was born in 1825.
French composer GEORGES BIZET, who wrote the opera "Carmen", was born in 1838.
New Zealand/Australian journalist STELLA ALLAN was born in 1871. Known as "Vesta" she introduced women's pages to Australia's newspapers.

Spanish painter PABLO PICASSO was born in 1881. He was one of the 20th century's most versatile artists gaining prominence as not only a painter but also a sculptor, graphic artist, ceramicist and designer.

Australian singer HELEN REDDY was born in 1942 into a show business family. She made her stage debut at the age of four. In the 1960s she had her own television show. She left for the USA in 1966 and had hits with "I Am Woman" (1972), "Delta Dawn" (1973), "Leave Me Alone (Ruby Red Dress)" (1973) and "Angie Baby" (1974).
British singer with 'Smokie' CHRIS NORMAN was born in 1950. Hits include "Living Next Door to Alice" (1976), "Lay Back In The Arms Of Someone" (1977) and "Oh Carol" (1978).
Australian actress SUSAN HANNAFORD, best known as "Kitty" in long-running "Sullivans" series, was born in 1953. She has also found success as a fashion designer.
Flying Doctors' star LENORE SMITH was born in 1958.
--EVENTS--
1415 : HENRY V of England defeated the French at the
Battle of Agincourt in northern France.
1760 : King GEORGE II of England died.
1839 : The world's first railway timetable was published
in Manchester.
1854 : In the Crimean War at the battle of Balaclava,
Lord CARDIGAN led the cavalry charge of the Light Brigade against the Russians, one of the most heroic episodes in British military history. 272 out of 673 were killed in the charge.
1900 : Britain annexed the mineral-rich territory of the
Transvaal.
1936 : Radio request programmes were born. A Berlin radio
station broadcast the first such programme called "You Ask - We Play".
1938 : Eighteen people were killed in one of Australia's

worst air disasters. Four crew and 14 passengers died when the Australian National airways Douglas DC2 ploughed into the Dandenong Ranges. The plane was en route from Adelaide to Sydney and was off course in heavy fog. The plane burst into flames on impact and wreckage was scattered over much of the mountainside.
1952 : The United States blocked Communist China's entry
to the United Nations for the third consecutive year.
1969 : The JOHN GORTON Liberal-Country party government
narrowly returned to power surviving an eight percent swing to Labor. The vote was seen as a victory for Labor leader GOUGH WHITLAM.
1971 : Taiwan was expelled from the United Nations to
allow the People's Republic of China to join.
1983 : Three days after the state election in Queensland,
Liberals DON LANE and BRIAN AUSTIN joined the National party giving the Bjelke-Petersen government a majority and the ability to rule in their own right.
1986 : Britain's satirical magazine "Private Eye"
celebrated surviving for 25 years. In the sixties editor RICHARD INGRAM decided to unearth and print the scandal and gossip that other papers would not touch.
1989 : ZSA ZSA GABOR was given three days jail, 120 hours

community work and fines for slapping a policeman, driving with an incorrect licence and carrying a flask of whisky in her Rolls Royce. The sentence from the weary Californian judge was criticised as a mere "wrist slap" for the star.
1994 : Stage and screen actor RAUL JULIA, best known from
the "Addams Family" movies and TV series, died at the age of 54.
